sections.h2: What does the Hunterdon County Clerk do when a house sells?
sections.html:
The County Clerk records the deed and the mortgage documents for a Hunterdon County sale, and the office describes itself as the keeper of the county's records. Its recording division checks each instrument for form, dates, signatures, acknowledgment and the location of the property. The recording fee and any transfer tax are paid to the clerk at the time of filing. The clerk then stamps the recording date, indexes the paper and abstracts every deed for the assessor of the municipality where the property sits. The original deed goes back to the owner.

The office is at 71 Main Street in Flemington, and the mailing address is PO Box 2900, Flemington, NJ 08822. Counter service runs weekdays, 8 a.m. until half past four, and the main number is (908) 788-1221. The clerk also publishes a notice about deed fraud and offers e-filing, so a title company or attorney handling your closing can submit digitally.

sections.h2: How much is the realty transfer fee in Hunterdon County?
sections.html:
The fee is set by state law and collected by the clerk on top of recording fees, at the moment the deed is offered for recording. The rate rises with the price, and it is stated per $500 of consideration or fraction of that amount. The schedule below is for a sale with total consideration above $350,000.

Realty transfer fee per $500 of consideration, sales above $350,000
Consideration bandFee per $500
Up to $150,000$2.90
$150,000 to $200,000$4.25
$200,000 to $550,000$4.80
$550,000 to $850,000$5.30
$850,000 to $1,000,000$5.80
Above $1,000,000$6.05

Source: NJ Division of Taxation form RTF-1EE (rev. 7/10/25), posted by the Hunterdon County Clerk.

Sales at or below $350,000 use lower rates. For a price over $1,000,000 on a residential property, the seller also owes the graduated percent fee, which starts at 1 percent of total consideration and climbs to 3.5 percent above $3,500,000. The county clerk's recording page says that deeds above $1,000,000 received after July 1, 2025 may be subject to a revised fee. A seller who wants an exact figure should use the clerk's realty transfer fee calculator.

sections.h2: Which Hunterdon County deeds are exempt from the transfer fee?
sections.html:
The state form lists exemptions, and a few cover situations that sellers and families run into. The fee does not apply to these deeds:

  • A deed for consideration of less than $100.
  • A deed from an executor or administrator to a devisee or heir that distributes the estate under the will or the intestacy laws.
  • A transfer between spouses or civil union partners, or between a parent and child.
  • A deed recorded within 90 days after a divorce decree ends the marriage.
  • A deed given only to provide or release security for a debt, and a deed that corrects or confirms an earlier recorded deed.
  • A deed on a sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.

An exemption has to be explained in detail on the affidavit. A simple exemption symbol is not enough.

The clerk will not record a deed unless it recites the consideration or carries an affidavit that states it. Consideration includes the money paid, the value of anything else given, and the balance of any mortgage the buyer assumes. Falsifying it is a fourth-degree crime under the state form's warning.

sections.h2: What do Hunterdon County's property tax rates look like?
sections.html:
The recording step connects to the tax bill because the clerk sends each deed to the municipal assessor. Hunterdon County has 26 municipalities, and the state's 2025 table shows effective tax rates running from 1.782 in East Amwell to 3.483 in Hampton. Flemington, the county seat, is at a general rate of 2.736 and an effective rate of 2.984. Lambertville is at 1.902 effective, Clinton Town at 2.808 and High Bridge at 3.152.

The effective rate puts every town on the same footing, so a low general rate does not by itself mean a low bill. Bethlehem Township shows a general rate of 2.021 and an effective rate of 2.350, while Milford shows 4.027 general and 2.944 effective. Look up your own municipality before you choose a list price.

Source: NJ Division of Taxation, 2025 General Tax Rates.

sections.h2: What is Hunterdon County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Hunterdon sits in western New Jersey and has 427.84 square miles of land, which gives it about 301 people per square mile. The Census Bureau estimates 131,781 residents for 2025 and counts 50,860 households. Owners occupy 85.1 percent of the homes, those homes are valued at a median $517,200, and a typical household earns $141,715. Gross rent in the middle of the range is $1,687. Residents 65 and older make up 23.4 percent of the population, and the county issued 544 building permits in 2025.

The Highlands cover the western third of the county and the Piedmont covers the rest, including the Hunterdon Plateau and the Raritan Valley Lowlands. The county was created in 1714 from Burlington County, and Flemington holds the county courthouse. NJ Transit's Raritan Valley Line serves High Bridge, Annandale, Lebanon and Whitehouse Station, and the county LINK offers demand-response service with fixed routes in Flemington. The average commute is 33 minutes.

Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts; Hunterdon County, New Jersey (Wikipedia).

sections.h2: How can a seller search Hunterdon County land records?
sections.html:
The clerk's records go back to 1785, and the Record Room is open to the public on weekdays. The Search Room is also open, and an appointment is available through the search room phone line at (908) 788-1380 for extra help. Older records are being redacted to protect identities, with an online system planned after that work ends.

Sellers use these records to confirm the vesting deed, find an open mortgage that needs a release, or locate a recorded lien before a closing. The clerk's recording page also links a homeowner's guide to good deeds, a document reference manual and mortgage foreclosure help for owners behind on payments.

Hunterdon County does not take part in the Homeless Trust Fund, a point the clerk's recording page notes for anyone budgeting fees.

sections.h2: What should I confirm with the clerk before closing?
sections.html:
• The current recording fee schedule, since only the transfer fee rates are reproduced here.
  • Whether the deed needs the Affidavit of Consideration for Use by Seller, which applies when the price tops $1,000,000 or an exemption is claimed.
  • Who signs the affidavit: the form allows a grantor, a legal representative, or a title or lending officer.
  • The method of delivery, in person, by mail or through e-filing.
  • The block and lot number, which the form requires and the municipal assessor can supply.

faqs.q: Where does a Hunterdon County deed get recorded?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's recording section, 71 Main Street in Flemington. Doors are open on weekdays until half past four, and the phone number is (908) 788-1221.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer fee on a Hunterdon County sale?
faqs.a: The seller's side pays it. The state form shows the fee as paid by the seller, and the clerk collects it with the deed at recording.

faqs.q: Is a deed from an estate to an heir exempt from the transfer fee?
faqs.a: Yes. The state form exempts a deed from an executor or administrator to a devisee or heir that carries out the will or the intestacy laws.

faqs.q: Which Hunterdon County town has the highest effective tax rate?
faqs.a: Hampton, at 3.483 in the state's 2025 table. East Amwell has the lowest at 1.782.

faqs.q: Can I look up old Hunterdon County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk's records start in 1785, and the Record Room and Search Room are open to the public on weekdays.
